## Finding

blocks-the-design

Named failure: unbound-unverifiable rapid pass.

A zero-verified acceptance walk exits 0 under rapid acOnly. Five clauses with `artifact_path: null`, evaluated on the check-integrated profile, returned ok with code 0. The pass lead was `verify:ac passed (#3284) (0 verified, 5 unverifiable) [rung=derived]`. Ceremony depth rapid resolved mode rapid and acOnly true, and the framework check list filtered to `verify:ac` alone.

Evidence. At aba2407f86bbef9b21f1b07d85ce396886d6bef5 this worktree ran two checks. `evaluateVerifyAcFromPlan` with `checkIntegrated: true`, `captureFromNarratives: false`, empty `commands`, and five unbound clauses returned `{ok: true, code: 0}` and that pass lead, with no FAILED line. `resolveProductFirstCheckMode` with `ceremonyDepth: "rapid"` returned `{mode: "rapid", acOnly: true}`. `applyProductFirstGateMode(FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES, "rapid")` returned `["verify:ac"]`. The same filter on `"pressure"` returned 48 gates, including `verify:branch`. The shipped test "still exits 0 on a no-oracle walk and leads with the counts" passed in `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/acceptance-resolver.test.ts`.

`walkOne` records a null artifact path as unverifiable and `adjudicable: false`. `walkAcceptanceClauses` is ok when nothing failed and `countUnverifiedAdjudicableClauses` is 0. `clauseWalkBlocks` returns false when `adjudicableUnverified` is 0. `clampVerifyAcExit` returns 0 when `ok` is true. `runCachedCheck` iterates that filtered list and takes `finish(0)` after a zero exit when the run is not toolchain-degraded.

Failure mode. Ceremony rapid makes `task check` a product-first authority stamp on a walk that verified nothing. The hygiene, branch, coverage, and suite gates are absent from the list that loop runs, so a zero-verified acceptance walk is a green check.

Disposition. The refutation target cannot bind. The pain on #4866 is this exit. A take that treats an unverifiable clause as a verify:ac failure, or that treats acOnly as a mode whose other gates still run, names a cause this tree does not execute.

## Existing mechanisms

#3284 rapid composition keeps the product AC gate (`applyProductFirstGateMode` in `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/check-mode.ts`; the loop is `packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts`). #3826 leaves a no-oracle clause unverifiable and non-adjudicable, so an all-unbound set can pass (`packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts`). #4380 prints the counts on that pass lead. `clauseWalkBlocks` in `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/acceptance-resolver.ts` blocks a failed clause, and an adjudicable clause that did not verify when no green executable run exists. #3497 is that shared predicate. `clampVerifyAcExit` in `packages/cli/src/verify-ac.ts` maps `ok` to exit 0.

## Road not taken

Pressure mode. `applyProductFirstGateMode` on `"pressure"` keeps the full framework list (48 gates on this tree, including `verify:branch`). Pressure sets `acOnly` false and continues after a hygiene failure because `hygieneAdvisory` is true. Rapid is the mode that sets `acOnly` true and drops those gates before the loop. The printed `acOnly=true` line is rapid.

## Steelman

The strongest reading of "unverifiable clauses fail verify:ac" is the #3497 wording that a clause the walk cannot decide blocks when nothing else verified the product. That reading would make this walk a failure. It flips if `clauseWalkBlocks` counts non-adjudicable unverifiable rows as `adjudicableUnverified`. The function counts adjudicable rows that are not verified. #3826 records why an empty oracle set stays a pass: requiring `verified > 0` from clauses that can only be unverifiable is unsatisfiable by correct work. #4380 kept that pass and moved the counts onto the lead.

## Footnote

footnote. A toolchain-degraded run whose every composed gate is skipped returns `finish(2)` before the walk. Under rapid the composed list is still only `verify:ac`. That exit is missing tooling. This critic measured the filter and the walk. `runCachedCheck` was read at the pin.

## Coverage

The bound remedy on comment 5779344810 covers pain P1 from the Stop 1 write-back 5779053609. The bind map can stay.

P1 is a rapid deft check that exits 0 after verify:ac reports zero verified clauses. Bound-remedy sentence 1 forbids that exit on a rapid product-first check when the acceptance walk reports zero verified clauses. Sentence 2 keeps the two refuted accounts out of the contract: unverifiable clauses already failing verify:ac, and the other gates still running. The exit change in sentence 1 is the relief.

## Evidence

At sha aba2407f86bbef9b21f1b07d85ce396886d6bef5 this worktree executed the pinned modules.

evaluateVerifyAcFromPlan with checkIntegrated true, captureFromNarratives false, empty commands, reuseMode never, and five clauses with artifact_path null returned ok true, code 0, resolution empty-pass. The pass lead was verify:ac passed (#3284) (0 verified, 5 unverifiable) [rung=derived]. The message contained 0 verified and contained no FAILED line. clampVerifyAcExit, taken from packages/cli/src/verify-ac.ts, returned 0 for that ok.

walkAcceptanceClauses returned 0 verified, 5 unverifiable, 0 failed, ok true, and every row adjudicable false. clauseWalkBlocks with failed 0, walked 5, adjudicableUnverified 0, and hasGreenExecutableRun false returned false.

resolveProductFirstCheckMode with ceremonyDepth rapid returned mode rapid and acOnly true. applyProductFirstGateMode on FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES for rapid returned [verify:ac]. The pressure filter returned 48 gates, including verify:branch.

runCachedCheck prints the product-first line from that mode resolution and returns finish(0) when the composed gate exits 0 and the run is not toolchain-degraded. Under rapid the composed list is that one gate.

## Existing mechanisms

ok stays true because clauseWalkBlocks does not block non-adjudicable unverifiable rows (#3826, packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/acceptance-resolver.ts). The pass lead is applied later and leaves ok and code unchanged (#4380, relabelVerifyAcPassLead). Rapid mode drops the other gates before the loop (applyProductFirstGateMode). clampVerifyAcExit maps ok true to exit 0.

Sentence 1 is met by a non-zero exit from the rapid check when the walk reports zero verified. Putting the pressure gates back on the list leaves this exit in place whenever those gates pass.

## Authority

The check exit is the authority stamp. Five null artifact paths, which are story input, are enough to reach ok true and exit 0 while rapid skips the rest of the list. Sentence 1 withdraws that stamp when the walk reports zero verified. The remedy adds no prompt, envelope, identity, worktree, or shared-state channel.

## Road not taken

Read sentence 2 as cancelling sentence 1, so the cite would only restate the refuted claim with both reasons withdrawn.

## Steelman

That reading is the strongest way to call the cite empty. The refutation target already said the rapid check does not exit 0, and the round-1 critic showed both because-clauses are false. Sentence 2 repeats that those accounts are false. What remains is sentence 1 as an outcome on the rapid check. This run showed that outcome is currently an exit 0 with a zero-verified report. The verdict flips if the rapid check can still exit 0 while the walk reports zero verified and sentence 1 is satisfied, or if the measured walk does not report zero verified. This run reported zero verified and exited 0. Sentence 1 names that pair.

## Footnote

footnote. Pass-lead edit. relabelVerifyAcPassLead leaves ok and code unchanged. A lead-only edit leaves the exit sentence 1 forbids.

footnote. Clause-less empty-pass. A walk with no clauses skips the count report and can still clamp to 0. Stop 1's because-clause is the walk that reports zero verified clauses. This run is that walk. The clause-less pass sits outside the report sentence 1 names.

Adoption blocker.

This is about Gates: the check that stands in the doorway before work is called good. A green result should mean Directive actually looked. A red result should say what to do next.

What a new person hits: With a story in progress, the main check prints success, verifies none of the acceptance criteria, and skips the tests and the branch rules.

Why that ruins the product for them: The moment they ask "is this actually ok" the product says yes without looking. Trust breaks on the first check.

How likely: High once they have any work in progress, which is the point of the first afternoon.

metadata.issueBody:
Parent: #4814

## Finding

With a story active, deft check printed product-first mode=rapid acOnly=true, verify:ac passed (0 verified, 5 unverifiable), and ran no tests, coverage, branch gate, or hygiene. The same repo with nothing active failed verify:branch.

Split out of #4814 so the parent stays a tracker and this failure can be triaged on its own. A fix for the other findings on that report would not close this one.

## Normalization

- Promise: GATES
- Priority: Urgent (audit scale S1)
- Source: #4814
